title: Structured Positive Journaling (the “SHIFT” Focus Journal) to Reduce Perceived Stress in an Anatomical Dissection Course—A Multicenter, Cluster-Randomized, Actively Controlled Study
summary:
Background
The anatomy dissection course in the early years of medical school is stressful for many students: For weeks, they grapple intensively with death and the human body while simultaneously facing significant academic and exam pressures. Regular journaling could help them cope with this stress. However, it remains unclear whether any benefits stem from specific reflective questions or from the act of writing itself.

Research Question
Does a structured journal with guiding questions reduce the experience of stress in the dissection course more effectively than a free-form journal without such questions?

Methodology
Participants are medical students from 5 different German universities enrolled in the dissection course. Entire course groups are randomly assigned in advance to one of two variants: a journal with structured guiding questions or a journal with blank pages. Both are offered to all course participants free of charge and on a voluntary basis.

Stress levels are assessed via a questionnaire at the start of the course, after approximately four weeks, and at the end of the semester if applicable. In addition, data on self-care, use and acceptance of the format, as well as general information, are collected; the diary entries themselves are not analyzed. Participation is voluntary and has no impact on the course or exams; the survey is conducted anonymously. In cases of very high stress, a predefined procedure for arranging support is implemented.

interventions.name:
A structured focus diary in paper format with guiding questions for
resource-oriented reflection, 2 times 3 minutes a day (morning and evening) for 4 weeks

The same paper format, but free writing without structured
reflection questions, 2 times 3 minutes a day (morning and evening) for 4 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Registration for the dissection course at the respective center; digital
informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of consent
• Age < 18 years
